list.description: Prometheus scraping the TON node metrics exporters
list.label: Prometheus
list.name: datasource
job
list.label: job
list.description: The scrape job to look at: one job is one network. Single-select on purpose — chain-level panels sum seqnos, block rates and collation budgets across whatever the selector spans, so a multi-job selection would merge unrelated fleets (mainnet + testnet) into one meaningless chain. Compare networks in two tabs.

list.name: instance
list.label: instance
list.description: Node filter within the selected job. Node and fleet-diagnostic panels respect it; chain-truth panels explicitly query every reporter in the job so selecting one node cannot redefine the blockchain.

list.name: agg
list.label: Node aggregation
list.description: How per-class and per-operation panels collapse selected nodes that expose the series: worst = maximum, p95 = the 95th percentile, median = the typical node, and best = minimum. Time-per-item panels include only nodes with traffic, where the ratio is defined. Health and tail panels keep their fixed aggregation. A ▾ in the title marks panels controlled by this selector.

list.name: perf_top
list.label: Perf series
list.description: Number of TD_PERF_COUNTER operations shown in each perf chart. Use 50 to include up to 50 registered operations.

panels.title: Actor CPU busy (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_worker_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker="cpu"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})) / on (job, instance) clamp_min(sum by (job, instance) (ton_actor_worker_threads{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker="cpu"}), 1))

panels.description: Worst selected node's CPU-worker occupancy from actor and coroutine dispatches, including elapsed time in the current dispatch. The outer dispatch scope includes signal-only work, gaps between handlers and finish bookkeeping. This is elapsed scheduler occupancy, not OS CPU; blocking inside actor code is included.

panels.title: Actor IO busy (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_worker_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker="io"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})) / on (job, instance) clamp_min(sum by (job, instance) (ton_actor_worker_threads{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker="io"}), 1))

panels.description: Worst selected node's IO-worker occupancy from actor dispatches, including elapsed time in the current dispatch. The outer dispatch scope includes signal-only work, gaps between handlers and finish bookkeeping. Each scheduler has one IO worker, so sustained pressure means moving work off polling actors rather than adding CPU workers.

panels.title: Local run queue (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (ton_actor_scheduler_local_queue_length{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.description: Largest selected target's visible runnable backlog, summed over its scheduler-local CPU queues. This is a lower bound because shared CPU and IO queues are not exposed. Nonzero on most scrapes indicates sustained CPU-worker saturation; an isolated sample can be transient.

panels.title: Longest running handler (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, max by (job, instance, actor) (ton_actor_scheduler_current_execute_seconds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.description: Point sample of the longest actor or coroutine dispatch currently in flight on any selected scheduler; the collecting worker is excluded. Yellow starts at 1 s and red at 5 s. The colors are diagnostic guides; treat red as a wedge only when it persists for several scrapes because a short spike can be a legitimate large actor batch or coroutine resumption.

panels.title: Max queue delay (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, max by (job, instance, type) (ton_actor_max_queue_ticks{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",window="recent"} / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})))

panels.description: Worst scheduling delay retained by two recent max buckets, converted from each target's raw ticks before taking the fleet maximum. The buckets are nominally 10 minutes at the assumed TSC rate; exact wall duration is platform-dependent. A spike cliff-drops when both buckets expire, which is a window artifact rather than necessarily an instantaneous recovery. Yellow starts at 100 ms and red at 1 s as diagnostic guides, not SLOs.

panels.title: Max executor drain (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, max by (job, instance, type) (ton_actor_max_execute_ticks{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",window="recent"} / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})))

panels.description: Worst timed executor drain retained by two recent max buckets. It covers signal/mailbox processing but excludes finish-time bookkeeping. The buckets are nominally 10 minutes at the assumed TSC rate; exact wall duration is platform-dependent. A spike cliff-drops when both buckets expire, which is a window artifact. Yellow starts at 100 ms and red at 1 s as diagnostic guides, not SLOs.

panels.title: Peak messages/s (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Actor-message and bare-coroutine throughput on the busiest selected target. Fleet sums scale with node count; this card highlights a hot node instead.

panels.title: Nodes without actor stats

targets.expr: (count(up{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} == 1) or vector(0)) - (count(ton_actor_stats_enabled{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} == 1) or vector(0))

panels.description: Selected, scraped-up targets that do not export enabled actor statistics. This includes an explicit disabled gate and older builds without the actor tier. Zero is healthy. A down target drops out of both terms; use TON Overview for target reachability.

panels.title: Worker occupancy by node/kind

targets.expr: max by (job, instance, worker) ((sum by (job, instance, worker) (rate(ton_actor_worker_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker=~"cpu|io"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})) / on (job, instance, worker) clamp_min(max by (job, instance, worker) (ton_actor_worker_threads{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance",worker=~"cpu|io"}), 1))

panels.description: Per-target CPU/IO worker utilization: outer actor/coroutine dispatch time divided by available threads of that kind, then the worst target for each node/kind. 1.0 is 100% pool occupancy. IO near 1 is the sharper alarm because each scheduler has one unsplittable poll thread. This is scheduler-group occupancy, not OS CPU; one saturated scheduler can be diluted by idle siblings. Blocking, signal-only work, gaps between handlers and finish bookkeeping are included. The counter includes elapsed time in the current dispatch; Longest in-flight execution is the companion wedge signal. Values can briefly exceed 1 after a thread-count change because the numerator is windowed and the denominator is instantaneous.

panels.title: Local run-queue by node

targets.expr: sum by (job, instance) (ton_actor_scheduler_local_queue_length{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})

panels.description: Runnable entries (actors with mail + resumable coroutines) in the per-cpu-worker work-stealing queues, summed per node. Lower bound on the backlog: the shared MPMC queue and the io queue expose no size, so work waiting there is invisible. Nonzero on most scrapes = cpu workers saturated.

panels.title: Longest in-flight execution by node

targets.expr: max by (job, instance, actor) (ton_actor_scheduler_current_execute_seconds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"})

panels.description: Point sample at scrape: of the other workers currently inside an actor or coroutine dispatch, how long the longest-running one has been at it. Dispatches shorter than the scrape interval are never seen — this catches a wedged or very long turn, not a duty cycle. The collecting worker is excluded. Each series is labeled with the (id-stripped) name of the actor holding the worker at sample time — during a wedge the rising line names the stuck actor directly.

panels.title: Actor handler load (${agg:text} node ▾)

targets.expr: quantile by (type) (${agg}, sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))) and on (type) topk(8, sum by (type) (increase(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end()) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (last_over_time(ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end()))))

(sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))) and on (type, job, instance) (bottomk by (type)(1, avg_over_time((abs((sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))) - on (type) group_left() (quantile by (type) (${agg}, sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))))))[$__range:] @ end()))) and on (type) topk(8, sum by (type) (increase(ton_actor_busy_ticks_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end()) / on (job, instance) group_left max by (job, instance) (last_over_time(ton_actor_ticks_per_second{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end()))))

panels.description: ▾ Handler or coroutine-resumption seconds per second for each class, computed per node and then collapsed with Node aggregation. Actor and coroutine samples enter when the handler or resumption returns; live outer-dispatch time remains visible in the worker panels. Nodes without that class are absent rather than zero. Blocking and descheduling are included, but signal-only work, gaps and dispatch bookkeeping are not, so this does not sum to worker occupancy. Top 8 classes by total busy time over the visible range. Hover attribution: the tooltip lists "class ⇒ node" rows (hidden from the chart) answering, per class, whose number the drawn line is. Each row names one stable node for the visible range — on a Node-switch panel the node whose series stays nearest the drawn quantile (the dominant node under worst, the node the median follows under median), elsewhere the node that dominated the range — and always carries that node's own value, so where the row hugs the drawn line, the line is that node.

panels.title: Actor messages/s (${agg:text} node ▾)

targets.expr: quantile by (type) (${agg}, sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (type) topk(8, sum by (type) (increase(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end())))

(sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (type, job, instance) (bottomk by (type)(1, avg_over_time((abs((sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) - on (type) group_left() (quantile by (type) (${agg}, sum by (type, job, instance) (rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))))[$__range:] @ end()))) and on (type) topk(8, sum by (type) (increase(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range] @ end())))

panels.description: ▾ Actor-message or coroutine-resumption throughput for each class, computed per node and then collapsed with Node aggregation. Nodes without that class are absent rather than zero. Compare with handler load: high throughput plus low load means cheap, frequent work. Top 8 classes by total messages over the visible range. Hover attribution: the tooltip lists "class ⇒ node" rows (hidden from the chart) answering, per class, whose number the drawn line is. Each row names one stable node for the visible range — on a Node-switch panel the node whose series stays nearest the drawn quantile (the dominant node under worst, the node the median follows under median), elsewhere the node that dominated the range — and always carries that node's own value, so where the row hugs the drawn line, the line is that node.

panels.title: Messages/s by node/kind

targets.expr: sum by (job, instance, worker) (rate(ton_actor_worker_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Actor messages plus bare coroutine resumptions per second, split by node and io/cpu worker kind.

panels.description: ▾ Follows the "Node aggregation" switch: each node keeps a retained maximum (~10–20 min window); the switch picks which node's retained max to show — worst (default), p95, median, or best. Largest number of messages drained in one executor batch for each class across the two recent TSC buckets; exact wall duration is platform-dependent. Use with Max executor drain: a high count with a short drain can be efficient amortization, while a high count with a long drain is head-of-line risk. There is no universal bad batch count, so this contextual panel deliberately has no alarm threshold. Hover attribution: the tooltip lists "class ⇒ node" rows (hidden from the chart) answering, per class, whose number the drawn line is. Each row names one stable node for the visible range — on a Node-switch panel the node whose series stays nearest the drawn quantile (the dominant node under worst, the node the median follows under median), elsewhere the node that dominated the range — and always carries that node's own value, so where the row hugs the drawn line, the line is that node.

panels.title: Alive actors (worst node)

targets.expr: topk(1, sum by (job, instance) (ton_actor_alive{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}))

panels.description: Highest actor count on any selected node. A rising floor over hours is a leak signal; using the worst node avoids diluting a one-node leak as the selected fleet grows.

panels.title: Weighted batch

targets.expr: sum(rate(ton_actor_messages_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(ton_actor_executions_total{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.description: Total completed work items divided by total executions across selected nodes: an execution-weighted batching ratio. Values above 1 mean scheduling was amortized over multiple messages; signal-only turns can make it fall below 1. No executions in the window renders No data.
